section: Basic Structure doctrine - evolution and content; Kesavananda Bharati and after (Indira Gandhi, Minerva Mills, Waman Rao, I.R. Coelho)
subsections: Basic structure doctrine - meaning, absence of definition, judicial review and supremacy debate

accepted.s: Which one of the following most accurately describes the basic structure doctrine?
o: The Supreme Court alone may amend the Constitution when required
Only the Preamble can be amended subject to judicial approval
Parliament may amend every constitutional provision without limitation
Parliament may amend the Constitution, but cannot damage or destroy its core features
accepted.x: The doctrine permits amendment of any part of the Constitution under Article 368, but prohibits alteration, damage or destruction of features that give the Constitution its identity.
accepted.tq: Choose the precise statement distinguishing the amending power from its constitutional limitation.
accepted.sec: Basic structure doctrine - meaning, absence of definition, judicial review and supremacy debate

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the basic structure doctrine:
1. It is expressly defined in a separate provision of the Constitution.
2. It was developed by the Supreme Court through judicial decisions.
3. Its content has evolved case by case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The doctrine is not expressly defined in the Constitution. It is judge-made and its elements have emerged progressively through case law.
accepted.tq: Identify the false statement carrying the textual-definition trap.
accepted.sec: Basic structure doctrine - meaning, absence of definition, judicial review and supremacy debate

accepted.s: With reference to the present position on constitutional amendments, which one of the following is correct?
o: Fundamental Rights may be amended only by an executive order
Fundamental Rights may be amended, provided the basic structure is not damaged
Fundamental Rights cannot be amended under any circumstances
Fundamental Rights are outside the scope of Article 368
accepted.x: Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights under Article 368, but the amendment remains subject to the basic structure limitation.
accepted.tq: Apply the rule to a specific constitutional component rather than recalling an isolated case name.
accepted.sec: Basic structure doctrine - meaning, absence of definition, judicial review and supremacy debate

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Preamble is a part of the Constitution.
2. The Preamble may be amended, subject to the basic structure limitation.
3. The basic structure doctrine means that only the Preamble cannot be amended.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Preamble is part of the Constitution and is amendable subject to the basic structure doctrine. Basic structure is not confined to the Preamble alone.
accepted.tq: Separate the true constitutional position from the restrictive ‘only’ formulation.
accepted.sec: Basic structure doctrine - meaning, absence of definition, judicial review and supremacy debate

accepted.s: The basic structure doctrine primarily rests on which constitutional principle?
o: Supremacy of Parliament over the Constitution
Supremacy of the executive over the legislature
Supremacy of conventions over written provisions
Supremacy of the Constitution and judicial review by the courts
accepted.x: The doctrine rests on the supremacy of the Constitution and the power of courts to review constitutional amendments against its basic features.
accepted.tq: Test the underlying constitutional principle rather than the name of the doctrine.
accepted.sec: Basic structure doctrine - meaning, absence of definition, judicial review and supremacy debate

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a reason why the Indian Parliament is not sovereign in the British sense?
o: Parliament possesses an unlimited amending power
The Constitution is written and supreme
accepted.x: Parliament does not possess an unlimited amending power. The written Constitution, Fundamental Rights, judicial review, federal division of powers and limited amending power restrict parliamentary sovereignty.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses a feature of the limited constitutional system.
accepted.sec: Basic structure doctrine - meaning, absence of definition, judicial review and supremacy debate

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The basic structure doctrine has been criticised as judicial rewriting of the Constitution.
Reason (R): The doctrine has no explicit textual definition and its content is developed by unelected judges case by case.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true. The absence of a textual definition and the open-ended judicial development of the doctrine form the basis of this criticism.
accepted.tq: Check whether the reason directly explains the criticism stated in the assertion.
accepted.sec: Basic structure doctrine - meaning, absence of definition, judicial review and supremacy debate

accepted.s: Which of the following is regarded as a defence of the basic structure doctrine?
o: It checks majoritarian misuse of Article 368 and strengthens constitutionalism
It makes Parliament sovereign in the British sense
It permits majoritarian misuse of Article 368
accepted.x: The doctrine is defended as a major contribution of the judiciary to constitutionalism because it checks the misuse of the amending power by a temporary majority.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the stated defence of a doctrine from its criticisms and legal effects.
accepted.sec: Basic structure doctrine - meaning, absence of definition, judicial review and supremacy debate

accepted.s: The Supreme Court held in Shankari Prasad (1951) that:
o: The basic structure doctrine applies to all Ninth Schedule laws
Article 368 includes the power to amend Fundamental Rights and an amendment is not law under Article 13
An amendment is law under Article 13 and cannot abridge Fundamental Rights
accepted.x: Shankari Prasad held that Article 368 covers amendments to Fundamental Rights and that a constitutional amendment is not ‘law’ within the meaning of Article 13.
accepted.tq: Match the earliest case with its specific holding and avoid later-case attributes.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Sajjan Singh — first application of the basic structure doctrine
Golaknath — Fundamental Rights are transcendental and immutable
Shankari Prasad — 42nd Amendment provisions struck down
accepted.x: Golaknath held that Fundamental Rights were transcendental and immutable, treated an amendment as law under Article 13, and held that Parliament could not abridge Fundamental Rights.
accepted.tq: Use the case-contribution pair and reject achievements belonging to later or different cases.

accepted.s: The dissent of Justice Mudholkar in which case first referred to the idea of ‘basic features’ of the Constitution?
accepted.x: Justice Mudholkar’s dissent in Sajjan Singh (1965) is noted as the first judicial reference to the idea of basic features.
accepted.tq: Test the precursor observation rather than the later case that formally propounded the doctrine.

accepted.s:
With reference to the Golaknath case, consider the following statements:
1. It overruled the earlier position in Shankari Prasad and Sajjan Singh.
2. It held that an amendment is ‘law’ under Article 13.
3. It was decided by an 11-judge bench by a 6:5 majority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Golaknath overruled the earlier position, treated an amendment as law under Article 13, and was decided by 11 judges with a 6:5 majority.
accepted.tq: Verify the case’s holding, effect on precedent and numerical bench details together.

accepted.s: The constitutional response to the Golaknath judgment was provided through which amendment, which amended Articles 13 and 368?
accepted.x: The 24th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1971 was Parliament’s response to Golaknath and amended Articles 13 and 368.
accepted.tq: Match the amendment number and year with the constitutional response to the judgment.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Kesavananda Bharati is correct?
o: It was decided on 26 January 1975 by a 13-judge bench by a 6:7 majority
It was decided by a 7-judge bench by a 6:5 majority in 1971
It was decided on 24 April 1973 by a 13-judge bench by a 7:6 majority
It was decided by an 11-judge bench by a unanimous decision in 1973
accepted.x: Kesavananda Bharati was decided on 24 April 1973 by a 13-judge bench with a 7:6 majority.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among closely related dates, bench sizes and majority figures.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Kesavananda Bharati:
1. It first propounded the basic structure doctrine.
2. It overruled Golaknath.
3. It upheld the 24th Constitutional Amendment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The judgment propounded the basic structure doctrine, overruled Golaknath and upheld the 24th Amendment.
accepted.tq: Combine the case’s principal doctrinal contribution with its treatment of the earlier judgment and amendment.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Case)
a. Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain
a. Minerva Mills
c. Waman Rao
d. I.R. Coelho

List-II (Contribution)
i. Ninth Schedule laws after 1973 became subject to testing
ii. Doctrine applies from 24 April 1973
 iii. First application of the doctrine and protection of free and fair elections
iv. Struck down clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368 inserted by the 42nd Amendment
accepted.x: Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain was the first application; Minerva Mills invalidated clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368; Waman Rao fixed 24 April 1973; I.R. Coelho made post-1973 Ninth Schedule laws testable.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure case-contribution pairs and eliminate codes that conflict with them.

accepted.s: In which case was the basic structure doctrine applied for the first time, with free and fair elections treated as a basic feature?
accepted.x: Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975) marked the first application of the basic structure doctrine, and the relevant clause of the 39th Amendment was struck down; free and fair elections were recognised as a basic feature.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the formal propounding of a doctrine from its first subsequent application.

accepted.s: The Supreme Court struck down clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368, inserted by the 42nd Amendment, in:
accepted.x: In Minerva Mills (1980), the Court struck down clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368 and reaffirmed judicial review, limited amending power and harmony between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.
accepted.tq: Match the challenged constitutional provision with the case that invalidated it.

accepted.s: Which case held that the basic structure doctrine applies to constitutional amendments made on or after 24 April 1973?
accepted.x: Waman Rao (1981) held that the basic structure doctrine applies from 24 April 1973, the date of the Kesavananda Bharati judgment.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive cut-off date to identify the relevant case.

accepted.s: What was the principal significance of I.R. Coelho (2007) in the development of the basic structure doctrine?
o: It declared all Ninth Schedule laws immune from review
It upheld the 17th Amendment without qualification
It made Ninth Schedule laws placed there after 1973 subject to basic structure review
It first recognised the Preamble as part of the Constitution
accepted.x: I.R. Coelho held that laws inserted into the Ninth Schedule after 1973 could be tested against the basic structure of the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Distinguish later application to the Ninth Schedule from the original articulation of the doctrine.

accepted.s: Golaknath challenged which constitutional amendment concerning State land laws placed in the Ninth Schedule?
accepted.x: The Golaknath case challenged the Seventeenth Constitutional Amendment, which concerned State land reform laws placed in the Ninth Schedule.
accepted.tq: Identify the amendment directly associated with the litigation instead of the later amendment enacted in response.
